subject: Polity
sub_topic: Standing committees and ad hoc committees

concepts.name: Classification of Parliamentary Committees: Standing vs Ad Hoc
key_dimensions: Definitional distinction: permanent/continuous nature of Standing vs temporary/purpose-specific nature of Ad Hoc
Basis of constitution: Rules of Procedure vs special motion/order in each case
Examples and sub-classifications within each type (Financial, DRSCs, Inquiry, etc.)
UPSC trap: Select Committee and Joint Committee are Ad Hoc, not Standing — commonly confused

concepts.name: Departmentally Related Standing Committees (DRSCs): Structure and Mandate
key_dimensions: Evolution: Originally 17 (1993), expanded to 24 (2004), recently restructured to 8 (2024 proposal context)
Composition: Members drawn from both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha; ratio and total strength (31 members)
Functions: Examination of Demands for Grants, Bills referred, annual reports — but cannot examine constitutional/statutory bodies' own legislation
UPSC trap: DRSCs cannot discuss matters under adjudication or matters of day-to-day administration

concepts.name: Financial Committees: Public Accounts Committee (PAC)
key_dimensions: Constitutional/Rule basis: Article 151 (CAG report) + Rules of Procedure; 22 members, Lok Sabha dominance
Chairperson convention: Leader of Opposition from Lok Sabha chairs PAC — post-1967 convention, not a rule
Role: Examines appropriation accounts and CAG audit reports; retrospective in nature (post-expenditure scrutiny)
UPSC trap: PAC does not question policy decisions per se; it examines whether money was spent as Parliament intended

concepts.name: Financial Committees: Estimates Committee
key_dimensions: Composition: 30 members, ALL from Lok Sabha only — Rajya Sabha has NO representation (key UPSC trap)
Function: Suggests economies, improvements in organisation; examines estimates before expenditure — prospective nature
Limitations: Cannot question policy underlying estimates; suggestions are not binding on the government
Comparison with PAC: Estimates Committee is forward-looking; PAC is backward-looking

concepts.name: Financial Committees: Committee on Public Undertakings (CPU)
key_dimensions: Composition: 22 members (15 LS + 7 RS); examines working of Public Sector Undertakings
Scope: Examines CAG reports on PSUs; cannot examine PSUs of Defence, atomic energy under security considerations
Distinction from PAC: PAC examines government ministries; CPU examines public undertakings/PSUs specifically
UPSC trap: CPU cannot examine matters of major government policy or day-to-day administration of PSUs

concepts.name: Select Committee and Joint Committee on Bills: Nature and Powers
key_dimensions: Ad Hoc nature: Constituted for a specific Bill; dissolves after submitting report
Difference: Select Committee = members of one House; Joint Committee = members of both Houses
Powers: Can summon witnesses, examine experts, call for papers — quasi-judicial in character
UPSC trap: Money Bills CANNOT be referred to a Joint Committee; only ordinary Bills can be so referred

concepts.name: Committee on Subordinate Legislation
key_dimensions: Separate committees in each House (not a joint committee); scrutinises delegated legislation
Examines whether powers delegated by Parliament are being exercised within the scope of delegation
Can examine rules, regulations, bye-laws, notifications made under delegated authority
UPSC trap: It does NOT examine the parent Act itself — only the rules/regulations framed under it

concepts.name: Business Advisory Committee (BAC)
key_dimensions: Composition: Chaired by Speaker (Lok Sabha) / Chairman (Rajya Sabha); includes leaders of various parties
Function: Recommends allocation of time for government and other legislative business in the House
Recommendations are advisory — not binding; Speaker/Chairman has final authority
UPSC trap: BAC does not decide on admissibility of questions or notices — that is the Speaker's prerogative

concepts.name: Rules Committee
key_dimensions: Chaired by the Speaker (Lok Sabha) / Chairman (Rajya Sabha) — same as BAC but different function
Considers matters of procedure and conduct of business; recommends amendments to Rules of Procedure
Distinction from BAC: Rules Committee deals with procedural rules; BAC deals with scheduling of business
UPSC trap: Amendments to Rules recommended by Rules Committee must be approved by the full House

concepts.name: Committee on Privileges
key_dimensions: Examines questions of breach of privilege of the House or its members; reports to the House
Composition: Speaker nominates members; chaired by Speaker in LS (not a member of the committee)
Quasi-judicial function: Can recommend punishment including reprimand, suspension, or expulsion
UPSC trap: The committee only investigates and recommends; the House itself passes the final order/resolution

concepts.name: Committee on Ethics
key_dimensions: Examines cases of unethical conduct, moral turpitude, or conduct unbecoming of a member
Distinct from Committee on Privileges: Privileges deal with legal rights; Ethics deals with moral/professional standards
Relatively recent: Rajya Sabha (1997), Lok Sabha (2000); not constitutionally mandated
UPSC trap: Recommendations of Ethics Committee are not automatically binding; House retains final authority

concepts.name: Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC): Ad Hoc Investigative Nature
key_dimensions: Constituted by a motion passed in one House and concurred by the other; classic Ad Hoc committee
High-profile examples: Bofors, Harshad Mehta scam, 2G spectrum — signifies political significance
Powers: Summon witnesses including ministers and officials; examine documents
UPSC trap: JPC findings are not judicially enforceable; they are recommendatory and presented to Parliament

concepts.name: Committee on Government Assurances
key_dimensions: Scrutinises assurances, promises, undertakings given by Ministers on the floor of the House
Tracks whether assurances have been implemented within reasonable time
Separate committees in each House; covers only assurances made in that respective House
UPSC trap: It does NOT examine policy commitments in Budget speeches — only floor assurances during Question Hour, debates etc.

concepts.name: Committee on Papers Laid on the Table
key_dimensions: Examines all papers/documents laid on the Table of the House by Ministers under statutory provisions
Checks whether the laying was done within prescribed time, in prescribed form, with required explanations
Distinct from Committee on Subordinate Legislation: This covers all papers, not just delegated legislation
UPSC trap: This committee does NOT examine the content/merit of the papers — only procedural compliance of laying

concepts.name: Consultative Committees: Nature and Distinction from Parliamentary Committees
key_dimensions: Constituted by Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs; NOT parliamentary committees in the strict sense
Provide a forum for informal discussion between Ministers and MPs on policies of respective ministries
Membership is voluntary; meetings held during session and inter-session periods
UPSC trap: Consultative Committees have no formal powers — cannot summon witnesses or call for papers unlike DRSCs

concepts.name: Quorum, Voting, and Procedural Rules in Parliamentary Committees
key_dimensions: Quorum: One-third of total membership of the committee (not half as in the House)
Sittings: Committees meet even during inter-session periods — unlike the full House
Secrecy: Proceedings are secret; members cannot disclose evidence before report is presented to House
UPSC trap: A Minister who is a member of a DRSC cannot participate in scrutiny of their own ministry's demands

concepts.name: Role of DRSCs in Pre-legislative Scrutiny vs Post-legislative Review
key_dimensions: Pre-legislative: Bills can be referred to DRSCs before passage — enables detailed clause-by-clause examination
Post-legislative: Examine annual reports and long-term policy implementation of ministries
Declining trend: Many major Bills (CAA, Farm Laws) bypassed DRSC scrutiny — debate on weakening of committee system
UPSC trap: Reference of a Bill to DRSC is not mandatory — it is at the discretion of the Speaker/Chairman or the House

concepts.name: Committee on Welfare of SC/ST and Other Committees on Specific Constituencies
key_dimensions: Joint Committee of both Houses; examines welfare measures for SCs and STs under Union and State governments
Can examine working of constitutional safeguards (Articles 17, 46, reservations) but cannot legislate
Similar committees: Committee on Empowerment of Women — examines legislation and policies affecting women
UPSC trap: These committees can only recommend; they have no executive authority and cannot override state legislation

concepts.name: Library Committee and House Committee: Internal Administrative Committees
key_dimensions: Library Committee: Joint committee; supervises Parliamentary Library; assists members in research — not a scrutiny body
House Committee: Looks after residential accommodation and other amenities for members
Distinction: These are service/housekeeping committees, not legislative/financial scrutiny committees
UPSC trap: These committees have no role in law-making or financial oversight — purely administrative in nature

concepts.name: Effectiveness and Critiques of the Parliamentary Committee System in India
key_dimensions: Strength: Enable detailed technical scrutiny impossible on the floor; bipartisan deliberation; pre-legislative input
Weakness: Non-binding recommendations; frequent bypassing of committee referral for important Bills; low attendance
Comparison: UK Select Committees have more teeth; US Congressional Committees central to legislation — India's are weaker
Reform debates: PRS Legislative Research data on declining Bill referrals; Second ARC and various committee recommendations on strengthening DRSCs
